description:
We are participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge, focusing on the "Field Resource Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data" challenge. 

Our collective technical stack combines solid backend fundamentals, web development, data analysis, and problem-solving. We are passionate about turning raw NASA Earth observation and satellite data into practical insights for modern agriculture, optimizing resource distribution, and tackling climate-driven farming challenges.
summary: Field Shift is an interactive agronomic GIS platform that transforms live NASA Earth-observation data into climate-resilient, 4-year crop rotation plans. Farmers and agronomists can draw custom field boundaries anywhere on the map, import GeoJSON parcels, probe point telemetry, or inspect six global agricultural regions. By combining NASA climate and soil-moisture baselines with weather forecasts and soil properties, the simulator evaluates 12 crops across water balance, nitrogen carryover, pathogen intervals, soil organic matter, and 4-year net margin. Field Shift helps growers replace water-depleting monocultures with adaptive rotations that protect soil moisture, restore soil health, and safeguard farm profitability under intensifying drought and heat.
details:
What Field Shift Does & How It Works

Field Shift is a browser-based agronomic GIS platform that turns live NASA Earth-observation data into 4-year (2027–2030) climate-adaptive crop rotation plans. Users can inspect global benchmark parcels (Ukraine, USA, Spain, Brazil, Kenya), draw custom field polygons directly on the map, import GeoJSON boundaries, or click any coordinate on Earth for an instant point telemetry probe.

For every parcel or probed point, Field Shift runs live API pipelines:

- NASA POWER (GEOS / MERRA-2): Fetches 1991–present monthly and trailing 365-day daily series to compute 10-year precipitation norms (PRECTOTCORR), 5-year warming anomalies vs. 1991–2020 baselines (T2M), exact >=30°C heat-stress day counts (T2M_MAX), recent 14-day root-zone and deep profile soil wetness (GWETROOT / GWETPROF), and physical FAO-56 Penman-Monteith evapotranspiration (ET) derived from NASA solar irradiance (ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN), relative humidity (RH2M), and wind speed (WS2M).

- Open-Meteo ECMWF: Provides live 7-day weather forecasts and topsoil moisture profiles across three depths (0–1 cm, 9–27 cm, 27–81 cm).

- ISRIC SoilGrids v2.0: Supplies 250 m soil texture (clay, sand), pH, and organic carbon (SOC) estimates.

Using these live baselines, the built-in agronomic simulator evaluates 12 crops across water balance, biological nitrogen carryover, Sclerotinia and pathogen return intervals, soil organic matter (SOM) trajectory, cover crops, and no-till practices. An optimization solver recommends 4-year sequences tailored to user priorities (Water, Soil, or Profit), with side-by-side comparison against traditional monocultures, portfolio-wide analytics, and exportable CSV, JSON, and printable agronomic reports.

Benefits & Intended Impact

Instead of relying on static regional averages or intuition, farmers and agronomists get hyper-local, satellite-backed decision support. Field Shift helps growers preserve subsoil moisture, cut synthetic nitrogen costs through legume pairings, mitigate heat and drought yield shocks, and quantify the 4-year financial upside of regenerative crop rotations.

Tools, Languages & Software Used

- Frontend & Simulation Engine: Vanilla HTML5, CSS3 (light/dark themes, responsive layout, full English and Ukrainian localization), and modular JavaScript (ES6+) running entirely client-side with in-memory API caching and localStorage persistence.

- Geospatial & Mapping: Leaflet.js for satellite/relief layers, polygon drawing, area calculation, and interactive point probing.

- Data APIs: NASA POWER REST API (monthly, daily, and climatology endpoints), Open-Meteo ECMWF API, ISRIC SoilGrids v2.0 REST API, and OpenStreetMap Nominatim geocoding.

- Hosting: Deployed on Vercel (https://nasahackaton-plum.vercel.app/).

Creativity & Key Factors Considered

- Bridging scales: Combining 30+ years of NASA climate trends, current root-zone moisture, and 7-day sowing forecasts inside one zero-backend web workspace.

- Agronomic realism: Accounting for soil available water capacity (AWC), crop rooting depth, heat thresholds, pathogen break intervals, and customizable Water/Soil/Profit weighting.

- Resilience & Usability: Parallel request deduplication, offline/rate-limit benchmark fallbacks, and an interactive guided tour so both agronomists and non-GIS users can explore fields immediately.

Super Intelligence (SI) Acknowledgment

AI coding assistants were utilized during development to accelerate frontend scaffolding, refactoring, and UI text localization.
